instruction:
Add a repo-hygiene rule: no tracked source file may contain a user-specific home path. A developer's local path embedded as a default works on their machine and silently breaks every other checkout, Linux, Docker and CI.

A test will scan every tracked `.py`, `.pyi`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`, `.cfg` and `.ini` file. It skips:
- anything under `docs/`, `.docs/`, `reference_material/`, `.claude/` or `.memories/`;
- the usual tool and cache folders (`.git`, virtualenvs, `__pycache__`, `build`, `dist` and so on).

It fails on any Windows user-home path (`C:/Users/<name>` or `C:\Users\<name>`), Linux `/home/<name>` or macOS `/Users/<name>`, including ones in comments and docstrings.

Find every such path in the tracked source and fix it properly:
- Scripts that hard-code a data or schema folder from an old checkout should take it as a command-line argument, with a default relative to the repository (via `Path(__file__)`).
- Stale example paths should be removed or replaced with generic ones.

If a literal really must stay, the line can end with `# pragma: allow-hardcoded-path`, but don't use that to avoid fixing real defaults.
pytest_args: not benchmark and not integration and not property

source.subject: add path-hygiene + cross-repo integration tests, audit protocol
